description: Standup reads your git commits and your agents' sessions and writes the end-of-day update you can no longer write from memory.

ui.aboutDescription: What {site} reads, what it writes and who made it.
ui.notFoundBody: This page does not exist. No commit made it, yours or an agent’s.
ui.aboutBody: {site} is a free plugin for coding agents with two skills, eod-review for a day and eow-review for a week or a month. Radu Ceuca built it at What Could Go Wrong to answer one question at the end of the day: what did I do.
ui.headline: You and your agents were busy all day.
ui.ledeMorning: It’s {time}, the team standup is in an hour and yesterday is a blur. Three agents kept working after you closed the laptop. Somebody will ask what you did. Standup reads yesterday back to you, your commits and theirs, before the coffee is done.
ui.ledeMidmorning: It’s {time}, you opened four Claude Code sessions before your first meeting and you have already lost track of which one is doing what. It is not even lunch. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work so far and tells you where the day stands.
ui.ledeAfternoon: It’s {time}, half the day is gone and it went somewhere. A branch you do not remember creating has six commits on it. They look fine, which is somehow worse. Somebody wants a status by end of day. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes down what has shipped so far.
ui.ledeEvening: It’s {time}, you have a dozen Claude Code sessions mid-flight, a handful of branches and no clear memory of the morning. How did we get here? Did we get anything done today? Manager asking for update. Client asking for status? You need to pick up your kid from acting classes in 1h. Standup goes through your work and your agents’ work and writes the summary for you.
ui.ledeNight: It’s {time}, you should be asleep and two agents are still going. By morning you will not remember what you asked them for. Go to bed. Standup reads the night’s work when you wake up and tells you what they did while you slept.
ui.installNote: Not published yet. These commands work once the repository is public. It reads files on your own disk and uploads nothing.
ui.receiptCaption: The numbers behind it, printed by the Alibi 3000
ui.readsBody: Standup gives you four to six lines you can say out loud. Paste them into Slack, say them at standup, or keep them as proof the day happened.
ui.weekTitle: On Friday, ask for the week.
ui.weekBody: eow-review covers Monday to Sunday day by day, and a whole month the same way. This is the week this page was built, three days in. Monday's work is still there on Friday, which is more than most of us can say.
ui.numbersTitle: It also says what the agents cost.
ui.numbersBody: Tokens are counted per folder, branch and day, dead ends included. The dollar figure is an estimate at API list prices, and the report labels it that way. On a subscription you pay none of it per token. It is still a number worth knowing before someone else asks.
ui.requirements: Needs Python 3.9 or later and git. Runs on macOS and Linux.
ui.askTitle: "What did you work on today?" is a hard question now.
ui.askBody: It used to be easy. You did one thing at a time and you were there for all of it. Now you start three things before lunch, an agent finishes two of them, and another runs in a worktree you forgot about. The work happened. You were not in the room for most of it.
ui.agentsTitle: It reads git and eight agents.
ui.projectsTitle: Work, consulting and side projects stay apart.
ui.projectsBody: Point it at the folder that holds all your repos and one report covers every project. Name your groups and each gets its own section, with its own commits and its own cost.
ui.installOther: Then ask it for today's EOD.
ui.agentPromptLabel: Or paste this into your agent
ui.agentPrompt: Read {llms} to learn what Standup reads and how to install it. Run the install command it lists for the agent you are. When it is installed, run eod-review for today and show me the report.
ui.exampleTitle: This is Wednesday 11 November 2026, the day this page was built. And its week, and its month.
ui.updateCaption: The update, as it pastes into Slack
ui.noteDate: The weekday is checked against the calendar before anything is written.
ui.noteLines: Eleven commits in three repos and three projects with no commit yet, grouped into six lines.
ui.noteStatus: 🔁 marks a merge, ✅ work finished here and 🚧 work still in progress, so nobody reads a merge as new work.
ui.noteFooter: The last line says where the work stands. Built is not the same as shipped.
ui.noteRepos: Commits come from git, from every branch of every repo in one folder.
ui.noteWork: Output and fresh input are what the models wrote and what they read for the first time.
ui.noteCache: 98% of the tokens are cache reads, billed at a twentieth of the input price or less.
ui.noteCost: An estimate at Anthropic's list prices, one price per model. A model with no listed price is counted and marked unpriced. On a subscription you pay none of it per token.
ui.closeBody: The update is written. The agents will keep going without you, and tomorrow Standup tells you what they did.
ui.noteUncommitted: A project with agent sessions and no commit is still listed, with how many files changed.
ui.voiceNote: A voice rewords each line. Names, numbers and status marks stay as they are.
ui.sourcesNote: What shipped comes from git, whoever wrote it, you or an agent. A session that Superconductor or Conductor ran in a separate worktree is followed back to its repo. Cursor and Antigravity keep no token counts on disk, so their sessions are counted.
ui.installCursor: Then turn Standup on under Plugins in Cursor, and ask it for today's EOD.
ui.installCopy: This clones the repository and copies the two skills into the folder your agent reads. Then ask it for today's EOD.
ui.homeTitle: {site}: daily standup plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
ui.agentExample: Read Wednesday 11 November as {site} wrote it
ui.claudeTitle: Daily standup plugin for Claude Code
ui.claudeDescription: {site} reads your Claude Code transcripts and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens and an estimated cost for every session.
ui.claudeBody: {site} reads the transcripts Claude Code keeps in ~/.claude/projects, and your git history, and writes what you and your sessions did today. Tokens are counted per folder, branch and day, with an estimated cost at Anthropic's list prices. Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days, so a report reaches back that far unless you raise cleanupPeriodDays.
ui.codexDescription: {site} reads your Codex sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with the tokens Codex used in each folder.
ui.codexBody: {site} reads the sessions Codex keeps in ~/.codex, and your git history, and writes what you and Codex did today. Codex records no branch, so its tokens are counted per folder and day. OpenAI's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.cursorDescription: {site} writes the day's update from every commit you and Cursor made, and counts your Cursor sessions. Cursor keeps no token counts on disk.
ui.cursorBody: Cursor keeps no token counts on disk, so {site} counts its sessions and takes the rest from git: every commit you and Cursor made today, on every branch. On a day spent in Cursor the token totals are lower than the truth. What shipped is complete either way.
ui.geminiTitle: Daily standup extension for Gemini CLI
ui.geminiDescription: {site} installs as a Gemini CLI extension. It reads your Gemini sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens per folder.
ui.geminiBody: {site} installs as a Gemini CLI extension. It reads the sessions Gemini CLI keeps in ~/.gemini, and your git history, and writes what you and Gemini did today. Tokens are counted per folder and day. Google's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.grokDescription: {site} reads your Grok sessions and your git commits and writes the day's update, with tokens wherever Grok's log records them.
ui.grokBody: {site} reads Grok's sessions and its usage log in ~/.grok, and your git history, and writes what you and Grok did today. Recent Grok versions may not write usage records; the setup check says whether yours does. xAI's models have no built-in price: the report counts their tokens and marks the cost unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.opencodeDescription: {site} is two skills you copy into opencode. They read opencode's database and your git commits and write the day's update, with tokens.
ui.opencodeBody: opencode has no plugin route for skills, so {site} is two skill folders you copy in. They read opencode's database in ~/.local/share/opencode, and your git history, and write what you and opencode did today. Claude models are priced out of the box. Any other provider's tokens are counted and marked unpriced until you add your rates to pricing.json.
ui.llmsAbout: {site} is a free, MIT-licensed plugin for coding agents. It has two skills: eod-review writes the update for a day, and eow-review for a week or a month. Both read git history and the session files your agents keep on disk, and open no network connection.
ui.llmsInstall: To install it, run the command for the agent you are. Then run eod-review for today.
